context.goal: 新型电力系统断面潮流控制：兼顾时效性、准确性、泛化性与可解释性，在实时运行和极端天气场景强化断面阻塞决策、确保安全裕度并适应电网动态演化。

reference_logic.mechanism: 把解释的可信度分解为三层并分别约束：第一层是依据可追溯，即对文献按段落与证据边界建索引，对运行参数按版本建独立知识，使每条解释都附带来源，从而压低无依据陈述；第二层是动作忠实，即文献检索只能保证“有出处”，不能保证解释与当前动作的实际电气效应一致，因此对关键动作构造可行的反事实（在保持功率平衡与设备边界的前提下替换或撤销动作，再重算交流潮流并比较关键支路），把解释中的方向描述与仿真里的动作效应绑定；第三层是人员效益，即解释是否真正帮助识别错误方案与缩短复核。中介路径为：有效证据覆盖与不适用规则过滤→解释方向与仿真一致→错误方案识别与复核效率。该机制的作用范围限于仿真内的动作效应检验，并明确不声称识别现实因果或提供安全保证；证据不足时输出“无法支持”，缺平衡资源的反事实判为不可检验。
reference_logic.evidence_needs: 需要四类可核查材料：(1) 带可追溯段落与合法访问来源的文献索引，用于支撑灵敏度方向、约束校验与交直流动作重算等具体断言；(2) 版本化的运行知识与拓扑配置，用以标记过期规则并支持知识版本过滤；(3) 固定候选方案集，须覆盖正确方案、方向错误、潜在新过载、过期拓扑规则和不可检验反事实五类，并配套统一潮流仿真与可用的平衡资源；(4) 双人独立标注及其一致性统计，以及人工复核时间与随机交叉顺序的实验记录。需要强调的是，文献只能支撑底层电气关系与约束校验，检索忠实性、反事实解释的增量作用和人工复核收益属于待检验命题，不能当作既有证据引用；引用支持率、方向一致率等指标本身也需在标注协议中先定义。
reference_logic.verification: 采用分层对照：至少200个固定候选方案的盲测集，按文档与拓扑分组留出以避免泄漏；对比无检索、仅检索、检索加反事实三组，并增设纯数值校核作为额外基线，以区分“解释起了作用”与“安全校核直接给出答案”。指标分别报告引用支持率、解释与仿真方向一致率、错误方案识别的精确率与召回率（在等误报率下比较召回）、解释延迟与人工复核时间。阴性判据预先设定：若引用支持率上升但忠实性无改善，或解释仅复述安全校核结论，则不成立反事实解释的增量贡献。人工部分采用随机交叉顺序控制学习效应，报告标注者间一致性，并在未完成人工实验时仅声明自动指标结论。
reference_logic.gaps: (1) 反事实依赖可行替代平衡资源，缺失时判为不可检验，导致可检验样本比例下降并可能引入选择性偏差；(2) 文献仅6篇，过期规则与拓扑不一致情形的覆盖偏窄，过滤率的估计不稳定；(3) 方向一致率是忠实性的代理指标，其构念效度未单独论证，且引用支持率与忠实性若由同一标注者判定存在混淆风险，需盲法与分人标注；(4) 固定动作集虽隔离了解释效应，但限制了对其他调控场景的外推；(5) 解释异步生成与独立安全校核并行的时序影响（如解释滞后导致的决策等待）未被量化为独立变量；(6) 未进入闭环下发，仅离线评估，生态效度与真实调度压力下的表现未知；(7) 人工复核收益受审核者背景影响，样本量与个体差异需要更大规模实验才能区分组间差异与噪声。

context.core_mechanism_constraint: 假设文献检索减少无依据陈述，但仅检索不能保证解释忠实于当前动作；反事实潮流干预将说明与实际电气效应绑定，从而揭示错误方向、过期规则或遗漏受影响线路。该干预用于检验仿真内的动作作用，不宣称识别所有现实因果效应。
existing_titles: 断面调控解释的反事实潮流忠实性假设：证据版本过滤与交流重算对错误方案识别的增益

queries: 反事实解释忠实性评估：通过交流潮流重算检验调控动作方向一致率，并考察其构念效度与双人盲法标注一致性（counterfactual explanation faithfulness: construct validity of action-direction agreement under AC power flow recomputation and blinded inter-annotator agreement）

可追溯证据与版本化规则过滤：检索增强解释的引用支持率、过期拓扑规则识别与不适用规则过滤效果评估（traceable evidence and versioned rule filtering: citation support rate, stale topology rule detection, and inapplicability filtering for retrieval-augmented explanations）

区分解释与安全校核：以纯数值越限校核作为额外基线，检验解释的增量贡献，并设计预先设定的阴性判据（distinguishing explanation from numerical security screening: an extra numerical limit-check baseline, incremental contribution testing, and pre-registered negative criteria）

断面阻塞决策中反事实的可检验性与选择性偏差：平衡资源约束导致的不可检验样本比例、可检验样本代表性及其外推限制（counterfactual testability and selection bias in congestion decision-making: untestable-sample proportion due to balancing-resource limits, representativeness, and extrapolation constraints）

极端天气与拓扑变化下的解释延迟与人工复核收益：错误方案识别精确率与召回率、复核时间的随机交叉实验设计及审核者背景影响（explanation latency and operator review benefit under extreme weather and topology change: wrong-plan detection precision/recall, review time, randomized crossover design, and reviewer background effects）

hits.text: 5UD08 ) 0 引言 高比例接入电网的风电 、 光伏等新能源具有间 歇性 ， 使得电网传输功率波动频繁 ， 容易造成线路 过载运行 。 过载线路故障跳闸会使潮流转移到关 联输电断面内其他线路上 ， 造成输电断面发生潮流 过载 ， 引起过载保护装置动作 ， 导致电网发生大规 模连锁跳闸事故 ， 严重威胁电力系统的安全稳定运 行 ［ 1-4 ］ 。 因此 ， 当电网面临切除过载线路引发输电 断面连锁过载的风险时 ， 调度人员应快速制定有效 的潮流控制策略 ， 紧急消除线路过载 ， 使电网恢复 到安全运行状态 ［ 5-7 ］ 。 目前消除线路过载的主要措 施为紧急调整发电机组出力和切负荷操作 。 潮流 控制策略主要包括灵敏度分析方法 ［ 8-13 ］ 和直接优化 类方法 ［ 14-18 ］ 。 文献 ［ 8-9 ］ 提出的灵敏度分析方法无须迭代 ， 不存在收敛性问题 ， 可以快速得到潮流控制策略 。 但是该方法仅考虑过载线路与调度节点之间的灵 敏度关系 ， 而电网具有高度非线性特征 ， 调度节点 会对其他线路的潮流有不同程度的影响 ， 可能会导 致新的线路发生过载 ， 须进行多次潮流校验 。 文献 ［ 10 ］ 基于交流潮流模型 ， 得到支路有功潮流对节点 有功注入的灵敏度 ， 通过节点有功灵敏度和负载率 等指标对输电断面潮流越限进行调度指导 。 但是 该方法仅提供调度人员指导建议 ， 没有给出消除输 电断面潮流越限的实际调度方案 。 文献 ［ 11 ］ 充分 考虑节点对过载及重载线路潮流的整体控制作用 ， 将综合灵敏度定义为节点对过载及重载线路灵敏 度的加权和 。 文献 ［ 12-13 ］ 提出基于综合灵敏度分 析的潮流越限切负荷调度方案 ， 但违背了机组出力 调整的优先级高于切负荷操作的原则 ， 会对供电可 靠性产生不利影响 ， 在实际电力系统调度中的应用 合理性有待检验 。 由于电力系统的非线性因素 ， 调 整发电机组出力以降低某些线路载荷的同时会增 加其他线路的载荷 。 如果不加筛选地利用综合灵 敏度指标来控制线路潮流 ， 可能出现某些机组节点 对群体线路的整体作用与对局部线路的作用相反 ， 部分控制节点被划分到出力调整效果加剧过载线 路越限的节点集合中 ， 导致优化算法需要更多的机 组节点参与调度以平抑不同机组的相互反作用 ， 不 利于潮流策略的制定 。 灵敏度分析方法将节点有功注入与线路有功 潮流间的非线性关系简化为线性关系 ， 当仅依靠灵 敏度关系通过多个控制节点来调整线路潮流时误 差较大 ， 难以达到实际电网的潮流控制精度要求 。 在输电断面潮流控制策略中 ， 文献 ［ 14 ］ 对比了灵敏 度分析方法和粒子群优化算法 ， 验证了基于粒子群 算法

hits.file: Interpretable Machine Learning Models for Critical Decision Systems
hits.text: ailable to humans. This paper is the systematic and complete study of interpretable machine learning models of critical decision systems. We start by examining the conceptual basis behind interpretability and its significance in high risk applications. An elaborate literature review classifies the currently existing interpretability methods as intrinsic interpretability methods and post-hoc explanation methods and their strong and weak points and the appropriateness to critical systems. The suggested methodology describes a systematic approach to the selection, design and validation of interpretable ML models within real-life conditions of uncertainties of data, bias and regulatory standards. Mathematically stated representative interpretable models such as linear models, decision trees, rule-based systems and attention mechanisms are given to provide formal grounding. Examples of experimental findings of representative domains of application are presented to illustrate the trade-offs in interpretability and performance. The discussion highlights levels of interpretability, robustness, and fairness measures, and predictive accuracy.

hits.file: Quantum-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Real-Time Dispatch in Hybrid Renewable Energy Grids
hits.text: The growing complexity of hybrid renewable energy grids, characterized by variable generation and decentralized assets, necessitates real-time decision-making frameworks that are both computationally efficient and operationally secure. This study proposes a Quantum-Augmented Reinforcement Learning (Q-ARL) framework to address the dispatch problem under network constraints and latency requirements. The conceptual analysis integrates quantum-safe infrastructure, control-theoretic AI safety, and statistical–topological learning foundations to construct a multi-layered architecture. The framework consists of (i) a real-time state estimation and forecasting layer leveraging IoT and SCADA streams, (ii) a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning dispatch layer coordinating system- and feeder-level decisions, (iii) a quantum augmentation layer that accelerates combinatorial action selection, variance-reduced value estimation, and state abstraction, and (iv) a security–verification layer

hits.text: ABSTRACT In recent years, intensifying global climate change has led to more frequent extreme weather events, causing abrupt fluctuations in electricity demand and renewable generation that threaten power system stability, especially under high renewable penetration. However, extreme weather data are often sparse, incomplete and discontinuous, posing significant challenges to load forecasting. To address these issues, this article proposes a general forecasting framework for extreme weather. The framework first applies a weighted dynamic time warping (WDTW)‐based sample selection method to identify historical samples similar to target extreme weather conditions, thereby enriching the training dataset. It then develops a deep learning‐based fine‐tuning strategy to enhance adaptability to extreme conditions while retaining the general feature extraction capability of the pre‐trained model. hits.file: Implementing Real-Time Edge AI for Anomaly Detection in Smart Grids: A Pilot Study on Power Distribution Networks
hits.text: In this pilot study, we aim to establish the changes needed to investigate whether edge AI can lead to real-time anomaly detection in the grid. In designing anomaly detection techniques, numerous other AI techniques such as artificial neural networks, among many others, have been investigated in previous works. However, only a few investigate their use for real-time anomaly detection in power systems. This pilot research looks into the possibility of developing a real-time anomaly detection methodology for smart grids. hits.text: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a Learning‐Augmented Distributionally Robust OPF (LA‐DROPF) framework for coordinated transmission‐distribution dispatch under deep uncertainty. The framework embeds GNN‐derived power flow sensitivities within Wasserstein‐metric DRO, where surrogate errors are absorbed by an inflated ambiguity radius. A hybrid Benders‐ADMM decomposition maintains inter‐operator privacy with convergence guarantees, and a CVaR layer controls tail voltage‐security risk. Finite‐sample guarantees ensure exponential decay of out‐of‐sample constraint violations, and an online mirror‐descent mechanism adapts the ambiguity set in real time. Experiments on 217‐bus and 630‐bus coupled systems—including tests with heterogeneous distribution feeder topologies—show that LA‐DROPF reduces DS‐level worst‐case cost by 33% relative to stochastic OPF and eliminates voltage violations that afflict deterministic and GNN‐only methods. hits.file: Power grid topology control
hits.text: Power grids are facing major challenges from growing renewable integration and worsening climate impacts. While flexibility on both the demand and generation sides has been widely explored to address these challenges, network-side flexibility, especially in network topology, remains highly underutilized. Advances in communication, power electronics, and circuit breakers have made network topology increasingly controllable. However, leveraging this topological flexibility poses substantial challenges, primarily due to the inherent non-convexity and hybrid dynamics in associated optimization and control problems. This monograph surveys the development of power grid topology control in both early and recent years. It begins by discussing the fundamental topological constraints involved in topology control problems. hits.text: ABSTRACT Under high‐penetration renewable energy integration, extreme weather events pose significant risks and challenges to power systems.
